crumb: 05 · The key ideas in one map
title: Hermeticism's key ideas in one map
desc: The working vocabulary of Hermetic thought in one connected map: Nous, gnosis, rebirth, correspondence, ascent — and how the pieces fit together.
tldr: Eleven concepts carry the whole tradition, and they form one machine: a cosmos born from Mind (Nous), knit together by correspondence, inhabited by a double human being whose task is transformative knowledge (gnosis) — achieved as rebirth, practised as ascent. Learn the map once and every text on this site snaps into place.
body:
You’ve read Poimandres. Before we go further into texts, let’s zoom out — because the Hermetica, for all their variety, keep running the same conceptual machine. Here is the whole map, one gear at a time.

The source: Nous

At the top sits Nous — Mind — which is both what God is and what God gives. Reality flows from it; revelation is it speaking. Everything else on this map is a way of getting back to it.

The fabric: correspondence

The cosmos hangs together by sympathy: correspondences bind stars to stones, heavens to bodies. This is what the famous “as above, so below” gestures at — and it’s why astrology and alchemy could count as sciences in this world: they read the threads.

The protagonist: the double human

From Poimandres you know the twist: humans are mortal by body, immortal by essence — the Asclepius goes further and calls the human a great miracle. We are the one being that stands on both floors of the building, which is why we alone can climb.

The goal: gnosis

Not information — gnosis: knowledge that transforms the knower. Its opposite in the texts isn’t ignorance but drunkenness, sleep, forgetting. The cure is waking up to what you already are.

The event: rebirth

Treatise XIII stages the change as palingenesia — rebirth — in which ten divine powers drive out twelve zodiacal torments. Count those numbers: liberation from astrology, argued in astrology’s own arithmetic. The map contains its own escape route.

The practice: ascent

And the route has stations: up through the spheres to the Eighth and Ninth, in prayer and song. A ritual text found at Nag Hammadi shows this wasn’t just imagery — someone practised it, together, with liturgy. The neighbouring name for practice-as-ascent is theurgy.

One warning label

The corpus is an anthology, not a system — some treatises love the cosmos, some fear it; scholars debate whether that’s contradiction or curriculum. Hold the map lightly. It’s a reader’s tool, not a creed — and now you own it.
facts: Nous → correspondence → double human → gnosis → rebirth → ascent

faq: It's our reader's map of recurring ideas — the ancient texts themselves never state a single system, and honest reading means keeping that in view.
Where do the 'seven principles' fit on this map?
They don't — they're a 1908 formulation from the Kybalion, not an ancient scheme. Step 10 tells that story in full.
Which idea should I explore first?
Nous — everything else on the map is downstream of it. Then follow your curiosity; the entries cross-link.
